ashby:alchemy:dce25389-91c4-4919-ac88-bc.summary:
Alchemy is the Web3 infrastructure and developer platform that powers millions of users and the world’s most innovative blockchain applications. From enabling $1+ trillion in financial transactions worldwide to scaling L2s and enabling DeFi, Alchemy provides the infrastructure and tools developers need to build reliable, scalable, and accessible experiences.

Trusted by companies like JPMorgan, Stripe, Visa, Franklin Templeton, Nike, and backed by a16z, Coatue, Silver Lake, Lightspeed, and Stanford University, Alchemy is building the foundational layer for a decentralized and AI-enabled Web3 ecosystem. For more information, visit alchemy.com .

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager, Platform to launch targeted campaigns across Alchemy's full platform, from product launches to new vertical and segment pushes, and to own the always-on content that fills the gaps in between. This is a high-ownership, high-influence seat with a long runway: you'll start as an executional hire, but there's a real path to Product Marketing Lead and to building a team under you if that's the direction you want to grow.

Alchemy isn't just infrastructure, it's a full platform: building blocks for reads, writes, launching custom chains, and more, spanning verticals from crypto-native builders to traditional finance moving assets onchain. Every campaign we run, whether it's a product launch, a new vertical push, or a piece of evergreen content, needs to tie back to one thing: Alchemy as the platform builders trust to build the future on. You'll own that positioning day to day, from the company-level narrative down to how a single launch is framed, working closely with Lisa (Product Marketing) especially early on as you build that domain authority.

You'll run point end to end: strategy, tactics, project management, measurement, and reporting, on everything from major campaigns to the product launches, newsletter beats, and social content that run continuously. You can and should delegate execution (design, technical content with DevRel, and more), but you own the outcome. When there's no active campaign, you're not idle: you own a pillar of Alchemy's always-on content, filling the gap with mid- and bottom-funnel work that drives activation and cross-sell across our existing platform.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Launch targeted campaigns across product launches and new vertical/segment pushes, owning the strategy, the tactics, and the project management from kickoff to report-out.

Own and evolve Alchemy's platform positioning: the throughline that connects every campaign back to Alchemy as a frontier leader built for reliability and performance, backed by real customer stories.
Own a pillar of Alchemy's always-on content cadence, mid- and bottom-funnel work, product launch beats, and activation/cross-sell content, whenever there isn't an active campaign in market.

Go deep on individual product areas and wide across the full platform, building the kind of product and audience understanding that lets you spot the next campaign or market opportunity before anyone asks for it.
Generate and pitch ideas for breaking into new markets and verticals, backed by a real read on the audience and the competitive landscape.
Partner with DevRel to produce the technical content (docs-adjacent explainers, videos, tutorials) that supports a campaign or fills a content gap.
Bring creative, visual thinking to launches that could otherwise be a dry API announcement, pushing for the campaign concept, not just the campaign checklist.
Delegate execution to design, agencies, and other specialists as needed, while remaining accountable for the outcome, the timeline, and the numbers.

sections.title: What we’re looking for
bullets: Experience selling to developers on a technical, API-first product with a developer dashboard, not a B2B SaaS platform candidates sign up for and self-manage. This is a hard requirement.
A track record of owning a campaign end to end: you can walk through, in detail, how you align stakeholders, launch, measure, and report on a campaign from a template through to results.
Genuine curiosity and a love of learning: going deep on a single product area and wide across an entire platform both excite you.
Creative instincts: you notice good brand and campaign work in the wild, and you bring visual or conceptual ideas that make a technical launch land.
Experience leading a large, high-visibility project end to end, e.g., a website overhaul, a rebrand, or a sales enablement overhaul.
Strong cross-functional operator: Product and Engineering partners trust you and want to work with you again.
Bias for speed and pragmatism: you default to "how do I get this out the door as fast and sharply as possible," not "how do I make this perfect."
Genuine enthusiasm for AI and how it's changing marketing and the developer tools landscape.

sections.title: Nice to Haves
bullets: Experience marketing to enterprise customers, especially financial services.
Breadth of experience marketing to developers across crypto/Web3 verticals.
Experience as a software engineer prior to marketing.
Leadership or management experience, or a clear interest in growing into it.

ashby:certifid:13d0f990-1cb0-473a-9e07-8.summary:
CertifID protects the money that moves in real estate. We help title companies, lenders, and their customers stop wire fraud before it happens, so every closing ends with funds in the right hands.

With our acquisitions of Closinglock and CloseSimple, we're now a combined team of roughly 240 people and one of the clear leaders in transaction security. We're scaling fast, integrating all 3 companies, and building the operating rhythm to match. That's where this role comes in.

sections.title: About the role
paras: The VP of Account Management owns revenue retention and expansion across CertifID's existing customer base. Reporting to our Chief Revenue Officer, you will set the strategy for how we grow within our accounts and build the team that delivers it.

This is a builder's role. You will build a dedicated Account Management function from the ground up, orchestrate cross-functional workflows across Sales, Product, and Post-Sales, and own Gross & Net Revenue Retention. You will be equal parts strategist, operator, and leader of people.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Own the expansion strategy. Define how CertifID grows revenue within existing customers through upsell, cross-sell, pricing and packaging, and multi-product adoption across our combined portfolio.
Own the number. Carry accountability for net revenue retention, gross retention, expansion bookings, and renewal rates. Build the forecast and run the business with rigor.
Build and scale the team. Hire, develop, and lead Account Managers and their managers. Set clear territories, segments, books of business, and compensation plans that reward the right behavior.
Segment and prioritize the base. Use data to tier accounts by revenue potential and risk, and match the coverage model to each segment.
Run a predictable renewal and expansion engine. Build account planning, QBR and executive sponsor programs, renewal playbooks, and pipeline management for expansion opportunities.

Partner across the business. Define clear handoffs and shared workflows with Sales and Post-Sales teams, collaborate with Product on customer feedback and roadmap input, and align with the CRO, Marketing, and RevOps on targets, tooling, and reporting.
Drive AI excellence. Define initiatives that leverage AI and the GTM tech stack to enable a best-in-class AM function, partnering with the data and RevOps team to deliver efficiency and productivity.
Be in front of customers. Build executive relationships with our largest and most strategic accounts and step into key negotiations.

sections.title: What you bring
bullets: 10+ years in B2B SaaS revenue roles, with at least 5 years leading Account Management, Customer Success, or Post-Sales revenue teams.
Direct ownership of an existing-customer revenue book between $75M and $250M, with a track record of growing net revenue retention.
Experience scaling teams through growth: hiring managers, building leadership layers, and growing headcount while keeping performance high.

An AI-forward mindset: you think strategically about how AI can reshape account management, and you build with it. Using AI tools and agents to sharpen account insights and automate workflows so your team spends more time with customers.
Operational rigor in forecasting, pipeline management, compensation design, and CRM-driven reporting.
A proven track record closing complex, multi-year renewals and expansion deals at the executive level.
A collaborative leadership style that builds strong partnerships with Sales, Post-Sales, Product, and Finance.

sections.title: Bonus points

You have integrated customer bases, teams, or product portfolios after an acquisition.
You have sold into or managed accounts in real estate, title and escrow, financial services, payments, or fraud prevention.

ashby:certifyos:0ec9dd90-fb56-4e4f-928a-.summary:

Our API-first platform automates provider licensing, enrollment, credentialing, and network monitoring by connecting directly to hundreds of primary data sources. We help healthcare organizations maintain accurate, compliant, and reliable provider networks at scale.

Our vision is simple: One API. One provider ID. Frictionless provider data.

paras: We’re backed by leading investors and built by a team with deep experience in provider data systems. At CertifyOS, we value authenticity, accountability, collaboration, results, and openness to feedback. sections.title: Solution design (about 70%)
bullets: Partner with Account Executives on mid-market deals as the technical lead from discovery through close.
Run discovery sessions with payer and provider organization stakeholders across credentialing, operations, IT, and compliance.
Map a prospect's current-state provider data workflows and design a future state on the CertifyOS platform, including where we fit and where we don't.
Scope integrations with client systems: APIs, file-based roster exchange, SFTP, and SSO.
Deliver tailored demos and produce client-facing solution design documents, scoping summaries, and RFP/RFI responses.
Bring what you hear from prospects back to Product and Engineering so it shapes the roadmap.

sections.title: Scaling Solutions Engineering with AI (about 30%)
bullets: Identify the highest-effort, most repetitive parts of the SE workflow, such as discovery prep, requirements extraction, RFP responses, solution design drafting, and demo setup.
Design, build, and maintain AI-powered workflows, prompts, and tools that cut the time and improve the consistency of that work.
Test what you build on your own deals first, then roll it out to the team with documentation and training.
Help turn one-off deliverables into reusable templates, playbooks, and a searchable knowledge base.
Track the impact of what you build, such as hours saved and turnaround time, and share results with leadership.

ashby:coderabbit:2db1c524-c15d-46b9-a14e.summary:
CodeRabbit is the governance and control layer for agentic software development, helping engineering teams trust the code they ship. AI can generate code faster than people can review and understand it. Teams still need to know whether each change solves the right problem, fits their architecture, and is safe to ship.

We provide independent validation grounded in codebase context and team standards, giving people the evidence they need to judge what should ship. Across Review, Triage, Explain, and Secure, our platform challenges changes before merge, prioritizes pull requests by value, impact, and risk, explains what changed and why it matters, and monitors the codebase for security vulnerabilities after merge.

CodeRabbit serves nearly 20,000 customers and supports approximately 300,000 open-source repositories, performing over 2 million code reviews each week. Our $143M Series C,…

sections.title: About the team
paras: CodeRabbit is the AI code review platform. Development teams install it on their repositories and it reviews every pull request, so it sits in the daily workflow of a large and fast-growing customer base. The Scaled Success team is responsible for the health of that base, and works alongside a program manager, a content and enablement specialist and a success analytics engineer. The pooled customer success team is new within it, and this is one of its first roles.

sections.title: The role
paras: You work a shared queue of customer accounts. Work arrives when a signal fires: onboarding has stalled, nothing has been configured, the only active user has gone quiet, a renewal is approaching, a cancellation has been started, or a team is using fewer seats than it has bought. You pick the case up, find out what is going on, get the customer configured and back to work, and close it out with a record the next person can read.

What you learn from the customers you work with feeds the playbooks, the automated campaigns and the triggers themselves. You work with the pooled team, the Content and Enablement Specialist, and the account executive who works expansion in the scaled lanes.

Few customer success teams run this way yet. You will learn how to move an account from default settings to a configured, renewing customer in a handful of conversations, and how to tell from the data which accounts need a person at all.

sections.title: What you'll own
bullets: The queue: pick up triggered accounts, respond within the team's standard, and resolve or route each one
Configuration: take customers from default settings to a setup that fits their repositories, including Path Instructions, Learnings, pre-merge checks, IDE and CLI, and MCP
Saves: work cancellation and non-renewal signals, understand the reason, fix what can be fixed, and record what cannot
Renewals: run the renewal conversation where the signals say one is needed
The expansion hand-off: when you see seat headroom or a buying signal, qualify it and pass it to the account executive with the context they need
Playbook feedback: every case the playbook did not cover becomes a note, and patterns across those notes become new content, a new trigger, or new automation
Case records: notes clean enough that anyone on the queue can pick up where you left off

sections.title: Your first quarter
bullets: Complete product onboarding and work your first cases alongside the team
Work the queue at the team's response standard
Document the first ten cases where the playbook was missing or wrong, and propose the fix for each
Contribute to the team's first readout: cases by trigger, resolution, and configuration movement on the accounts you touched

ashby:decagon:0e8a35cd-be75-436e-8407-f4.summary:

sections.title: About The Team

sections.title: About The Role

About Delinea:
Delinea is the identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long. It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Delinea provides visibility across every identity type, scores the risk each one carries, and preserves the context behind access decisions, making them auditable and defensible. It supports both static and ephemeral access, letting teams apply Zero Standing Privilege where risk demands it without replacing existing infrastructure.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

paras: The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Ramp's Enterprise Customer Success Managers on the Lifecycle team don't stop at go-live — they make sure customers keep getting more from Ramp as their business grows. Ramp has grown its product suite significantly over the last several years. As we've matured as an organization, our customer relationships have grown more complex too: customers are buying more of the platform at once, running it across more entities and teams, and relying on it for more of how their finance function operates. Hitting an activation milestone doesn't mean the job's finished. Too often, a feature that could solve a real problem goes unused because no one is there to show how it would work in that customer's business.

That's where you come in. This is a role for people who understand how finance teams actually run, who think in years rather than quarters, and who already use AI the way surgeons use instruments: not occasionally, not as an experiment, but as the default way they work. You'll own the customer experience after implementation for a book of Ramp's highest-potential enterprise customers, partnering with Account Management on long-term account strategy. sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own the post-implementation experience for a book of enterprise customers, with clear accountability for sustained adoption, customer satisfaction, and renewal readiness

Drive sustained adoption by understanding each customer's goals and guiding them toward the workflows that improve outcomes for their business — including the products and features they've already purchased but haven't fully put to work

Act as each customer's expert in finance workflows: understand how they run their business, advise on decisions as their needs change, and make the value of new Ramp capabilities clear in their context
Build multi-threaded relationships across every account and partner with Account Management on executive relationships, so the account stays steady through change like a new Controller or CFO

Partner with Account Management on QBRs and executive business reviews, quantifying Ramp's impact in the language CFOs and Controllers care about — close cycle improvement, spend visibility, savings, and ROI — not just product usage metrics
Spot opportunities for growth and bring them to Account Management, who owns renewals and expansion; as customers add products, drive ongoing activation so they reach value quickly
Run your book on data: monitor usage, CP, and risk signals, get ahead of challenges and escalations, and see them through to resolution well before renewal is on the calendar
Use AI tools daily to prepare for customer calls, build materials, synthesize data, identify account risk, and operate at a pace traditional methods can't match

sections.title: Must-Haves
bullets: Long-term account ownership — You've owned a book of customers past launch and through renewal, and you have measurable retention, adoption, or satisfaction results to show for it. Finance or fintech context is a plus but not required.

Customer experience mindset — You measure success by how customers feel about working with you, not only by milestones hit. You get ahead of problems before customers raise them and own escalations through resolution.
Executive relationship building — You build multi-threaded relationships across finance, operations, and the C-suite. When your champion leaves, the account doesn't leave with them.

Financial impact communication — You can walk a CFO through the value Ramp has delivered, connect adoption to P&L outcomes, and help make the case for continued investment in financial terms, not product terms. A finance background is not required — fluency is.

Data-driven book management — You prioritize your time based on usage, revenue, and risk signals, not on who emailed last. You can spot an at-risk account months before renewal and know what to do about it.

Technical and systems acumen — You're comfortable around major ERP platforms (NetSuite, SAP S/4HANA, Workday, Sage Intacct, or similar) and understand how Ramp fits into a customer's finance stack. Builder mindset — You're energized by building something that doesn't exist yet. This team is new, and you'll help shape the playbooks, programs, and rituals that define how Lifecycle CSMs work, all while running your own book. You bring structure to ambiguity and iterate quickly when something isn't working.

7+ years in enterprise customer success, account management, or consulting — You've spent enough time with complex organizations and senior stakeholders that it's second nature. You know how to keep an enterprise customer successful long after the launch.

ashby:siro:89967d63-9647-4d6a-9ef1-8c07e.summary:
Field sales powers the economy — but most teams are struggling. Reps are buried in admin work, managers are stretched thin, and leaders can’t see what’s really happening in the field.

Siro is redefining how field sales teams learn, perform, and win.

We started as an AI-powered coaching platform that helped reps improve their outcomes in the field.

Today, we’re something much bigger — an intelligent companion that automates sales reps’ tedious admin work, gives managers real-time visibility, and helps executives see around corners.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
paras: We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own meaningful pieces of Siro end-to-end — across AI, data ingestion, proactive agents, integrations, and the experiences customers touch every day.

Siro is building the intelligence layer for the enormous part of the economy that still runs on in-person conversation — an in-person workforce most software has ignored. We capture what happens in the field and turn it into intelligence our users act on daily — prepping a rep before a meeting, surfacing the next move, handling the follow-up.

Your job is to push that arc forward: make the intelligence sharper, make people trust it, and close the gap between insight and action. You'll own real problems the whole way, from ambiguous idea to a product customers rely on.
bullets: Own and ship end-to-end . Drive strategy and product concepts through discovery, launch, adoption, and iteration. You're on the hook for whether it provides value, not just whether it shipped.

Build for someone who doesn't sit at a desk. Our users are in trucks, driveways, and showrooms. We believe that we should never add work to a rep's day — the product has to earn its place, which makes this a harder and more interesting design problem to solve.

Be a forward-deployed PM. Our customers run businesses that look very different from ours and likely from any you’ve ever worked in. You'll get on the plane, ride along on calls, sit with managers onsite, listen to conversations, and turn what you learn across industries into one coherent product.

Move Siro from insight to action . Apply our intelligence to drive behavior change and operate the sales motion — prep before a conversation, the next move surfaced in the moment, the follow-up handled. This is where the product is heading, and you'll build it.
Raise the AI quality bar. Accuracy, citations, speaker attribution, latency, trust, the weird edge cases. A demo that impresses is easy; a tool a skeptical rep opens every morning is the actual job.

sections.title: Requirements / Who You Are
bullets: 6+ years in product management , including ownership of meaningful product areas at a growth-stage company.

You're a “ barrel.” Give you an ambiguous problem and you create momentum: figure out what matters, talk to the right customers, pull the data, make the tradeoffs, align the team, and get something valuable shipped. You don’t need a clean brief or constant direction to turn a vague opportunity into a real product.
Sound product judgment in messy domains . You're comfortable when the inputs are imperfect and there's no obvious right answer, and you pull the right people together to make good decisions.

Bias to action and doing whatever it takes. If you see friction in the UX or a customer complains about something on a call that you think is worth fixing — it’s not a ticket to an engineering backlog, you write the code and ship it.
Obsessed with customers and details. You'd take a day in the field over a day in a planning doc, and you make it happen without being asked.
Enough technical fluency to dig into the tradeoffs with engineering. model quality, latency vs. cost per query, and how fresh integration data really needs to be.

You carry product vision with you everywhere. You have strong taste, you think in systems, and you can connect today’s bug, customer ask, or workflow edge case to where the product needs to go over the next few years.

sections.title: Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
paras: Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:
bullets: No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

Please always verify communications:


• Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com .

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

greenhouse:cloudflare:8243552.summary: At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: As a Product Manager at Cloudflare, you will be responsible for building products that improve the way that the Internet works. Product Managers at Cloudflare shape high-level product goals but also get our hands dirty. On an average day, you might pitch a concept to senior leadership, collaborate with marketing, work with designers to conduct user research, prototype a new feature, iterate on a spec, analyze usage data, and pair with an engineer on implementation.

We are seeking a strategic and technical Senior Product Manager to lead the vision, strategy, and evolution of our Threat Intelligence portfolio. Your mission is to ensure Cloudflare’s security products and customers can identify, understand, and respond to emerging threats earlier and with greater confidence. You will own the end-to-end roadmap for the platforms, data, and workflows that transform Cloudflare’s unique network signals and security research into timely, actionable intelligence, balancing speed and coverage with accuracy, context, and low false-positive rates.

You will translate a rapidly evolving threat landscape, from emerging attacker infrastructure and campaigns to new tactics, techniques, and procedures, into scalable capabilities that improve detection and response across Cloudflare’s security portfolio. You will serve as a bridge between threat researchers, intelligence analysts, engineering teams, and market-facing functions, working closely with Sales, Customer Success, and our customers to understand their challenges and drive adoption. Your success will be measured by the quality, timeliness, and actionability of our intelligence and its impact on customer security outcomes.

sections.title: You will:
bullets: Own your space. You will own the priorities and scope for a high performing engineering team focusing on detecting advanced threat actors.

Connect the pieces. Product managers are a nerve center at Cloudflare, responsible for connecting engineering, program management, marketing, revenue, and partners to make sure that our ships go out on time and with the maximum impact.

Excel across teams. Enterprise capabilities cut across all of our product verticals, so you should be comfortable working with product managers across the company to prioritize systemic improvements that our enterprise customers need.
Be customer obsessed. You will be responsible for directly engaging with customers and understanding how they use our products. You’ll bring these insights back to the team to build a great roadmap.
Join pre-sales and post-sales calls with customers, sales, support, etc., to assist with, and help understand all phases of the customer lifecycle
Be data driven. You should be comfortable working with data, and analyzing data to quantify the impact of problems and opportunities in your space.

SPINS brings deep category and retail intelligence to this shift: attribute data, retail measurement across hundreds of retailers, and 30 years of insight into the values-based consumer, the growing group of shoppers who prioritize wellness, social responsibility, and sustainability. Through recent acquisitions and product investment, we’ve grown from a data and insights company into a broader CPG growth and innovation platform spanning commerce enablement, media, measurement, and AI-powered discovery, connecting insight to action across the path to purchase.
We’re looking for a Sr. Director of Product Marketing to lead marketing for the products shaping our next chapter, and to help define the categories they compete in.

This isn’t a caretaker role. Our newest platforms (AI-powered product discovery, agentic commerce readiness, connected commerce enablement) are creating markets that didn’t exist two years ago, and well-funded AI-native competitors are moving fast. We’re looking for a leader who has built a category story before and can do it at the pace the AI era demands, while keeping our established products differentiated and growing.
bullets: Lead the market narrative for how AI and agentic commerce are reshaping how brands get discovered, chosen, and bought.
Craft positioning that works on two fronts: differentiating our emerging AI products from fast-moving startups, and our established platforms from legacy incumbents.
Shape how products come together into a customer-centric portfolio story, with messaging tailored to the segments and industries we serve.
Lead, inspire, and develop the PMM team as SPINS scales into new markets, modeling AI-native ways of working and using AI to accelerate what the team delivers.
Build a culture of strategic thinking and high performance; recruit, mentor, and grow talent whose influence extends across the company.
Own product marketing strategy across the portfolio, balancing investment between scaling new platforms and extending established leaders.
Build a GTM engine suited to our pace: fast, repeatable launches, product-led growth alongside enterprise sales, and narratives that scale with the portfolio.
Bring customer and market insight back into product strategy, pressure-testing new ideas and spotting the next category opportunity.

sections.title: What SPINS Offers
paras: We have enjoyed tremendous growth over the years and, as a leader in a fast-growing industry, we have no plans to slow down! While all that growth brings excitement, it is also an opportunity for SPINS to show it values the health and wellness of its team members.
bullets: We embrace hybrid work options so that you have the flexibility to create a work/life balance that actually works!
Each employee is allotted paid time to use to volunteer with an organization of their choice and charitable donations are matched.
Semi-annual company-wide employee survey that is used to shape company programs, perks, and culture.

sections.title: The SPINS Way
paras: For details about the information SPINS’s collects about our applicants and how we use it, please see the SPINS Privacy Policy here .
bullets: Direct – We communicate with clarity, honesty and respect in all situations and embrace opportunities to provide solution-oriented feedback.
Determined – We are committed to overcoming all obstacles to achieve results. We adapt to change, seek opportunities to learn and rapidly translate that learning into action.
Passionate – We go above and beyond to help our partners achieve their goals. We challenge assumptions and are comfortable forging new paths.
Collaborative – We leave our egos at the door, believing that working together we will produce an outcome that’s greater than each individual contribution.

greenhouse:stratolaunch:5475102008.summary:
Stratolaunch accelerates the development of next-generation aerospace and defense technologies through reusable hypersonic flight testing. Our autonomous, air-launched Talon-A vehicles provide access to operationally realistic flight environments at speeds exceeding Mach 5, delivering critical data that helps customers validate system performance and advance technologies toward deployment. Our team brings together expertise in engineering, manufacturing, and flight operations to solve complex challenges and advance capabilities essential to national security.

The AI Solutions Engineer contributes to the development, integration, and operation of AI capabilities across Stratolaunch. The Enterprise Software Team integrates a mix of COTS and custom tools to provide the right data, functionality, and AI-enabled capabilities to the right user at the right time.

sections.title: ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES
bullets: Design, deploy, and operate reliable infrastructure for ML, LLM, and RAG workloads, with a focus on running and optimizing models in AWS and supporting future AI compute requirements.

Host, maintain, monitor, and optimize RAG systems, including Qdrant and other retrieval infrastructure, while developing the logging, observability, and alerting needed to assess system health, performance, cost, and reliability.
Serve as a subject matter expert for MLOps and AI workload operations, including model deployment, inference services, resource utilization, and production support.
Integrate and support COTS products, third-party services, open-source tools, and custom AI capabilities, sharing responsibility for their monitoring, security, cost, performance, and reliability.
Develop APIs, plugins, and reusable integrations that make AI capabilities available to Stratolaunch teams, including tools for OpenWebUI, Hugging Face, Wilbur, and other applicable platforms.

Collaborate with internal stakeholders to develop team-specific AI integrations and workflows, and to deliver practical interfaces between AI services and existing applications, including frontend applications, Streamlit services, NGINX load balancers, and other web infrastructure.
Collaborate with software, data, infrastructure, security, and domain teams to evaluate AI technologies and deliver maintainable, user-focused solutions.

sections.title: QUALIFICATIONS
bullets: Experience designing, deploying, and operating reliable, observable software or ML systems in production.
Experience with ML workloads, cloud infrastructure, and model deployment, preferably in AWS.
Experience with one or more programming languages, such as Python, Rust, C, MATLAB, or equivalent.
Experience developing and integrating APIs, services, plugins, or other software interfaces.
Experience with containerization, deployment, and orchestration technologies such as Docker, Kubernetes, Dagster, or equivalent tools.
Experience with logging, monitoring, troubleshooting, and production support.
Comfort with CLI tools and shell scripting, such as Bash or Windows batch scripting.
Knowledge of DevSecOps and CI/CD systems, such as Jenkins, GitLab, Bamboo, or equivalent tools.

sections.title: EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE
bullets: BS in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field, or applicable experience in lieu of degree.
5-10 years professional experience in software engineering, cloud infrastructure, data engineering, MLOps, AI engineering, or a related discipline.

greenhouse:stripe:8306158.summary:
Radar helps businesses prevent fraud and abuse without getting in the way of legitimate customers. We combine machine learning powered by Stripe’s global network with intuitive dashboard experiences and developer APIs, to give our users comprehensive controls and insights to protect their business against threats ranging from payment fraud and card testing to bot and free trial abuse.

Fraud doesn’t stand still, and it isn’t limited to checkout. As businesses launch new products and business models, attackers find new ways to exploit them. We obsess about understanding those attacks, identifying defenses that work, and making sophisticated fraud prevention simple for the businesses that depend on us to help them protect and grow their revenue with confidence.

sections.title: What you’ll do
paras: As a product manager on the Radar team, you’ll work directly with customers to understand the novel fraud and abuse attacks they face, identify the most important problems to solve, and turn those insights into product strategy and a roadmap.

You’ll work at the intersection of customers, engineering, data science, design, and commercial teams to shape what we build and bring it to market. Your work will span the fraud and abuse detection and control capabilities at the heart of Radar and the user and developer experiences that put those capabilities into our customers’ hands.
This role requires both urgency and taste. You’ll move quickly as threats evolve, without compromising on reliability, craft, or the details that make complex products feel beautifully simple.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Develop a deep understanding of the fraud and abuse landscape.
Investigate emerging attacks with customers, assess their financial and operational impact, and distinguish isolated incidents from opportunities to build broadly useful defenses.
Translate findings into a product strategy and roadmap, prioritizing the defenses that deliver the greatest customer and business impact.
Partner with engineering, data science, and design to explore signals, shape solutions, and rapidly turn effective defenses into scalable, reliable products.
Set the pace for the team by scoping the product thoughtfully, prioritizing ruthlessly, and executing with high rigor.
Work with sales, marketing, and customer-facing teams to validate demand, coordinate launches, and help customers adopt and maximize the value they get from new capabilities.
Own product performance, user experience, and business metrics to guide iteration and communicate progress.

sections.title: Who you are
paras: We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

sections.title: Minimum requirements
bullets: 8+ years of Product Management experience

Highly analytical, with a rigorous approach to quantitative and qualitative evidence. You’re comfortable digging into data, writing SQL when needed, and defining metrics that connect product decisions to user outcomes.
Scrappy and resourceful, with experience taking products from zero to one. You find ways to test ideas quickly, learn from real users, and turn early solutions into products that scale.
Strong commercial and business acumen. You understand how customer problems translate into willingness to pay, adoption, and durable business value.
Proven cross-functional leadership, including experience partnering with B2B sales teams on customer discovery, product positioning, and adoption.
Experience shipping Dashboard and API products, with empathy for both end users and developers and an understanding of their different workflows.
Comfort with substantial ambiguity. You can set direction with incomplete information, make thoughtful trade-offs, and adapt as new evidence emerges.
Technical fluency to go deep with engineering and data teams on complex systems, understand constraints, and evaluate alternative approaches.

sections.title: Who We Are:
paras: At Ai2, our mission is to develop breakthrough AI that solves the world's biggest problems. We believe the insight needed to get there lives at the intersection of deep scientific AI understanding and the application of AI in common-good domains. This role sits on our Strategic Programs team, which also includes Product Management, Design, and Communications. As a team, we help shape Ai2's strategic vision and accelerate execution of its goals. We are a highly collaborative team with a high bar for excellence, who aren't afraid to question how things have been done in the past to propose changes that drive the organization forward. It's a very exciting time to be part of this team as Ai2 plays a unique role in shaping how AI changes the world.

sections.title: Your Next Challenge:
paras: You will own the engineering and data frameworks of Asta, Ai2's platform for building agents that advance scientific research. Your users are the researchers and engineers who build on Asta; Ai2's own research teams and the broader AI-for-science community. Your primary partner will be the Agentic Frameworks and Data engineering team. You'll be one of the first product minds shaping what an agentic platform for science actually looks like. There's no existing playbook to inherit, so you have the opportunity to define engineering requirements grounded in real researcher workflows, build the roadmap for Asta's agentic framework and its supporting tools, and run the feedback loop that keeps engineering and research in continuous conversation. You'll also own the Semantic Scholar data platform end to end; a knowledge graph of 100M+ papers, and the public APIs that power Asta and science agents. You’ll keep these resources reliable for the millions who depend on it and continue building them into the highest-quality open literature resource in the field.
bullets: Define Asta engineering requirements by working directly with Ai2 researchers to understand their workflows, translating what you learn into clear, prioritized specifications for the Agentic Frameworks engineering team.
Help articulate trade offs to help guide the team towards the highest impact priorities and investments.
Build and sequence the roadmap for Asta's agentic framework and its supporting tools, so that new tools and capabilities compound toward unlocking real scientific advancements.

Create and run a continuous feedback loop between engineering and research, so that researchers’ needs surface early and shape the roadmap, and so that new capabilities get back in front of researchers quickly.
Drive adoption of Asta's tools among Ai2's own researchers, so that our internal science runs on the platform we ship to the world.

Project manage and drive execution across Asta engineering workstreams: track progress against the roadmap, unblock dependencies, and keep engineering and research aligned on priorities and tradeoffs.
Own the Semantic Scholar platform end to end: data platform and public APIs. Balancing reliability for millions of users with the roadmap to rebuild the platform.

Own Ai2's benchmarking strategy for scientific agents: set the direction for AstaBench, our public benchmark suite, and define which evaluations Ai2 standardizes on internally, with partners, and for the broader AI research community

sections.title: What You'll Need:
bullets: Bachelor's degree and 5-8+ years of product management experience, including shipping developer-facing or research-facing products such as APIs, platforms, or tools built for technical users.
Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous, research-driven needs into concrete engineering requirements and a sequenced roadmap.
Experience partnering closely with an engineering team on a technical platform, including day-to-day prioritization and execution, not just quarterly planning.
Genuine interest in AI research, agentic systems, and their application to scientific discovery, with the ability to learn a technical domain quickly.
Comfort owning compliance-related product requirements (e.g., data access, deletion, and privacy regulations) and translating them into engineering work.
Strong written communication — you can write a requirements doc, a roadmap update, and a risk escalation that people actually read and act on.
Excellent stakeholder management across research and engineering, including with senior leaders, and comfort navigating disagreement to a decision.
Comfort operating with ambiguity and building product processes where none exist yet, while knowing which processes are worth the overhead.

sections.title: Physical Demands and Work Environment:
bullets: Must be able to remain in a stationary position for long periods of time.
The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.
The ability to observe details at close range.
Can work under deadlines.

greenhouse:thrivecart:5476686008.summary: ThrivePages lets digital creators and online merchants build sales pages, landing pages, and funnels with checkout built in, without code or a designer. We’re looking for a Product Manager to work on features end to end and make building and converting with pages measurably better.

sections.title: Job Overview:
paras: You’ll work on features from discovery through launch and iteration. You’ll work daily with engineering, design, QA, and support. About 75% of your time is hands-on building: specs, prototypes, rollout plans, and release follow-through. The rest is deciding what comes next. You’ll work AI-first, using AI tools daily for research, specs, and prototypes.

sections.title: What You'll Do:
bullets: Define the user problem, success metrics, and trade-offs for your feature area, then run discovery through interviews, data, prototypes, and experiments.
Write PRDs and tickets with clear objectives, non-goals, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and a rollout plan.
Build a clickable prototype with AI for every feature. Engineers build from your prototype, not from a meeting.
Keep your product queue ranked and trusted, so nobody has to ask what’s next.
Decide how each feature rolls out (who gets it, behind what gate), and set up monitoring and analytics before launch.
Keep help docs, release notes, and internal enablement accurate.
Evaluate where AI genuinely helps users. Write evaluation criteria and a fallback before building any AI feature.

sections.title: What You Bring To This Role:
bullets: 3–5 years of product management experience, with a record of shipping features that solved real problems and moved a measurable metric.
Strong discovery and analytics skills. You pull your own numbers and design clean experiments.
Specs and prototypes that need no interpretation.
You’re comfortable reading code with an AI agent and tracing a feature from request to database. You can set up test data and run the product yourself without waiting on engineering.
Working knowledge of AI concepts (prompts, tokens, models) and the cost and latency trade-offs behind them.
Clear, high-signal communication across product, design, engineering, and support.
Experience with page builders, funnel or checkout tools, or products used to sell digital goods online is a plus.

sections.title: What Success Looks Like:
paras: Your features move a measurable metric. Engineers are unblocked because your requirements and decisions are clear. You’ll be the go-to person for your product area and ready to own a full roadmap.

greenhouse:tomorrow:8202855003.summary:

Enterprise CSMs play a strategic and hands-on role managing high-value, complex customer accounts across a variety of industries. In this role, you will operate with autonomy to drive measurable outcomes tied to customer success, adoption, and long-term value.

You will collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Marketing, Product, and Enablement teams, serving as the primary relationship manager and strategic advisor to your customers. You will bring a consultative approach to growth planning, executive engagement, risk mitigation, and lifecycle management.

sections.title: What you'll do:
bullets: Diagnose account health across complex enterprise accounts and proactively design success plans, renewal strategies, and multi-quarter adoption roadmaps aligned to customer goals and business value.
Deliver strategic QBRs and executive business reviews across multiple stakeholders that demonstrate ROI and shape customer transformation using weather intelligence.
Anticipate and mitigate risks to retention , using customer insights, adoption signals, and lifecycle data to guide intervention strategies.
Lead product enablement conversations by connecting use cases to value, delivering tailored walkthroughs, and translating roadmap changes into actionable plans for the customer.
Manage cross-functional alignment by collaborating with Account Management, Product, Science, and Enablement teams to resolve customer blockers, influence roadmaps, and build repeatable success.
Influence expansion opportunities by identifying whitespace, advocating for deeper platform adoption, and partnering with Sales to shape commercial strategy.
Troubleshoot customer challenges, and escalate feedback to internal stakeholders, ensuring swift resolution and continuous improvement.
Contribute to scalable Customer Success programs by developing or improving playbooks, templates, and internal processes used across the CSM team.

Strong strategic thinking, with the ability to tie product usage to business outcomes and confidently lead conversations with VP- and C-level contacts.

From cutting-edge weather intelligence to real-time early warning systems, Tomorrow.io enables predictive, impact-based action for a safer, more resilient future. Learn more at Tomorrow.io.

This portfolio includes enterprise retail software, Loss Prevention, Produce Recognition, video and computer vision solutions, vision analytics, and emerging AI-enabled retail and store-operations capabilities. lever:havenparkcommunities:f5d48caa-77f6.summary:
Data first . AI here runs on governed, well-defined data. When an agent needs a metric or a record, it should return the same answer the executive dashboard does, and when the data is not there yet, we expect you to say so and help get it there.

AI-accelerated, human-owned . AI is a fundamental part of how we work and how a small team builds things that scale across the portfolio. Use it in your own work every day, and keep a person accountable for every consequential decision.

Ship small, then scale . We deliver in pull-request-sized steps, start in development, and prove reliability before widening the audience.

sections.title: Building AI solutions
bullets: Assess how work is actually performed, role by role, and prioritize where AI removes steps rather than only speeding them up, weighing hours returned, error reduction, and how many people the change reaches.
Design, build, and ship AI companions, agents, and workflow automations from prototype through production, for users including selling agents, community teams, accounting, and marketing.

Integrate with the systems where work happens: HubSpot, Microsoft 365, Snowflake, our property management and finance platforms, and vendor APIs. Choose the runtime that fits the workload rather than forcing everything into one tool.
Build on the governed data models and semantic layer the analytics team maintains. You consume them rather than own them, and you tell us what agents need.
Maintain reusable patterns, prompts, tools, and evaluation sets so the third solution is faster to build than the first.

sections.title: Operating what you build
bullets: Own evaluation, monitoring, exception handling, and escalation for every production workflow. Define what good looks like before launch and know within hours when something drifts.
Enforce human review for consequential actions. Anything touching a customer, a resident, money, or a record of record keeps a person in the loop until the evidence says otherwise.
Manage model usage and cost, ship through source control and pull requests, and document each solution well enough that someone else could support it.
Keep the inventory of agents, prompts, and integrations current, including who owns each one and what it can access.

sections.title: Working with the business
bullets: Partner with function leaders to pick the right problems, agree on what success means, and confirm the value was realized after launch rather than at the demo.
Embed with users while a solution is new. Watch how they use it, find where it fails or gets ignored, and iterate. Adoption is part of the job.
Train users and their managers on what a solution does, what it does not, and how to escalate when it gets something wrong.

sections.title: Governance and security
bullets: Work within Havenpark's AI usage policy and bring new tools and use cases through the intake process, involving Legal and HR early when a use case touches applicant, resident, or employee data.
Give every agent and integration its own identity with least-privilege access. No shared API keys, no over-permissioned service accounts, and no production credentials in code.
Log what agents did, what data they used, and who approved consequential actions, so any outcome can be traced and explained.

US – Seattle only :

This position is open to candidates in the Seattle, WA area. You will have a hybrid remote/in-office schedule where you will work from our casual, pet-friendly office at least 3 days a week (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday).

Trupanion is further enhancing its native iOS and Android member app, and we are looking for a Senior Technical Product Manager to own it from launch through scale. You will set the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Core Member App, turning member insight, business goals, and technical realities into a mobile experience that lets pet parents submit and track claims, manage their policy, handle billing and payments, and get help, all from their phone.

sections.title: Job Description
paras: Working at the intersection of product, engineering, design, and the business in a regulated insurance environment, you will partner with mobile and platform engineering, an external development partner, and teams across Marketing, Member Experience, Finance, Legal, and InfoSec. You will define what success looks like (adoption, engagement, self-service deflection, retention, and app quality), make the hard trade-offs, and guide the app from MVP launch into a multi-phase roadmap that expands Trupanion’s digital ecosystem.
bullets: Product vision and strategy – Own and evolve the vision, strategy, and multi-phase roadmap for Trupanion’s native iOS and Android member app, aligning it to enterprise priorities in member engagement, retention, digital self-service, and growth.

MVP launch and parity – Lead the app through MVP launch, ensuring parity with the existing member web portal while delivering high-impact mobile enhancements across claims, policy, billing and payments, account management, and help and support.

Roadmap and prioritization – Build and maintain a phased roadmap (e.g., live chat, in-app enrollment, add-a-pet, expanded push notifications, digital wallet payments, digital pet ID, and claim pre-approvals), prioritizing with data-driven frameworks, business cases, and stakeholder input.

Requirements and backlog – Translate strategy into epics, user stories, user story maps, and clear acceptance criteria; own backlog health and sprint-to-roadmap alignment with Agile delivery teams and external development partners.

Member insight and discovery – Conduct customer and market research, competitive analysis, and journey analytics to identify member pain points and opportunities; partner with UX to validate concepts through prototyping, usability testing, and experimentation.

Metrics and outcomes – Define and own product KPIs such as app adoption, monthly active members, self-service and claim-submission rates, contact-center deflection, app store ratings, retention, and stability targets (99.5%+ crash-free sessions); use telemetry and product analytics to monitor performance and drive continuous improvement.

Release and app store management – Lead release planning and launch readiness for iOS and Android, including App Store and Google Play submissions and listings, phased rollouts, OS-version support, feature flags, and post-launch monitoring and hotfix prioritization.

Compliance, security, and accessibility – Ensure the product meets privacy, data protection, and security requirements (including PII encryption and device-integrity controls), WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards, app store policies, and English and Canadian French localization, working closely with Legal, Compliance, and InfoSec.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: Education – Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Information Systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Experience – 7+ years of product management experience with increasing responsibility, including at least 4 years owning consumer-facing native mobile apps (iOS and Android) from discovery through launch and ongoing iteration.

Mobile launch track record – Has taken at least one native mobile app or major mobile release to production through the App Store and Google Play, with accountability for adoption, ratings, and stability metrics.

Technical proficiency – Working knowledge of mobile app architecture, RESTful APIs, BFF patterns, authentication and identity, push notifications, and integrating third-party SDKs and services; able to read API documentation and partner credibly with engineers on technical design.

Tools – Hands-on experience with Jira and Confluence (or similar), product analytics and observability tools (e.g., Amplitude, Mixpanel, Firebase, or DataDog), and App Store Connect / Google Play Console.

Delivery methods – Proven experience with Agile/Scrum delivery, backlog governance, user story mapping, writing acceptance criteria, and release management across multiple teams, including external vendors or agencies.

Specialized knowledge – Familiarity with data privacy and security requirements (e.g., GDPR, PII handling), mobile accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA), and app store review and compliance guidelines.
Experience in insurance, fintech, healthcare, or another regulated industry, especially claims, billing, or payments experience.

sections.title: Additional Information
bullets: The base salary range for this position is $160,000 - $180,000 on a full-time schedule.
Along with base compensation, Trupanion employees are currently eligible for monthly bonuses.
We want all employees to be invested in Trupanion’s success, so we grant Restricted Stock Units to all new team members. Our new hire grants vest over 4 years.
